name: Francis Shoemaker
bio: a Representative from Minnesota; born on a farm in Flora Township, Renville County, Minn., April 25, 1889; self-educated with mother's assistance; engaged in agricultural pursuits and worked for many farm and labor organizations; charter member and organizer of the Minnesota Farmer-Labor Party; assisted in organizing the Federated Farmer-Labor Party at Chicago in 1923; editor and publisher of the People's Voice, Green Bay, Wis., 1921-1927, and of the Organized Farmer, Red Wing, Minn., in 1928; unsuccessful Farmer-Laborite candidate for election to the Seventy-second Congress in 1930; convicted on November 17, 1930, of mailing libelous and defamatory content; received probation but was revoked and sent to federal prison; pardoned by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on July 8, 1933; elected as a Farmer-Laborite to the Seventy-third Congress (March 4, 1933-January 3, 1935); was not a candidate for renomination in 1934 to the Seventy-fourth Congress, but was an unsuccessful Farmer-Laborite candidate for nomination for Senate; then became an unsuccessful Independent candidate for reelection to the Seventy-fourth Congress; unsuccessful Farmer-Laborite candidate for nomination to the Seventy-fifth Congress in 1936; unsuccessful Farmer-Laborite candidate for nomination to the Seventy-sixth Congress in 1938; unsuccessful Farmer-Laborite candidate for nomination to the Seventy-seventh Congress in 1940; unsuccessful Farmer-Laborite candidate for election to the Seventy-eighth Congress in 1942; unsuccessful Republican candidate for nomination to the Eightieth Congress in 1946; unsuccessful Democrat-Farmer-Laborite candidate for nomination to the Eighty-second Congress in 1950; unsuccessful Democrat-Farmer-Laborite candidate for nomination for Senate in 1952; resumed agricultural pursuits near North Redwood, Minn.; died in Minneapolis, Minn., July 24, 1958; interment in Zion Cemetery, Flora Township, Renville County, Minn.
